statement: The Colorado Privacy Act applies to a controller that conducts business in Colorado or produces or delivers commercial products or services that are intentionally targeted to residents of Colorado and that satisfies one or both thresholds: it controls or processes the personal data of 100,000 consumers or more during a calendar year, or it derives revenue or receives a discount on the price of goods or services from the sale of personal data and processes or controls the personal data of 25,000 consumers or more (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 6-1-1304(1)).
caveat: § 6-1-1304(2) carves out listed data and entities (GLBA financial institutions and data, HIPAA-governed health information, FCRA activities, employment records, data under named federal regimes, certain state bodies, and others), and amendment versions shown on the mirror extend the part to a controller that processes biometric identifiers or biometric data in any amount, for the biometric provisions, without regard to these thresholds. Statutory text verified on the FindLaw mirror; confirm against the official Colorado Revised Statutes before relying. This repo does not determine whether the Act applies to a given business.
